organizations.canonical_name: Norwegian Armed Forces High Command, Fourth Office (FO IV)
organizations.normalization_notes: The historical Norwegian name is preserved. FO IV was a wartime office of the Norwegian Armed Forces High Command; it is not silently merged into OSS.
The publication title is preserved as documented by City College. The evidence supports an editorial and publishing affiliation, not an inferred modern corporate successor.

affiliations.role_title: Head of the Fourth Office (FO IV)
affiliations.research_notes: The institutional biography places Øen in FO IV from 1942 and documents its wartime liaison role. The exact formal transition into the OSS-indexed relationship is not stated, so the temporal basis is strongly date-bounded rather than explicit immediate.

The rare exact name and the role's 1937 start support a qualified prewar affiliation, but the accessible source does not directly bridge this biography to the OSS file or establish that the publication was Offin's immediate predecessor.

claims.claim_text: Bjarne Oen's best-supported immediate pre-OSS military assignment was leading the Norwegian Armed Forces High Command's Fourth Office (FO IV).
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Store norske leksikon states that Øen led FO IV from 1942, connecting Norwegian resistance work with British special operations during the wartime period represented by his OSS index file.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the distinctive name, Norwegian spelling variant, and compatible senior wartime role.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded: FO IV leadership began in 1942 and continued during wartime Allied coordination, but the source does not state a formal OSS recruitment date.
claims.match_notes: FO IV is preserved as a Norwegian military assignment and is not mislabeled as a civilian employer or silently merged into OSS.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Edward W Oexner is probably the World War II Army master sergeant documented in a Veterans Affairs-derived national-cemetery transcription.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The unusual exact name and Army master-sergeant status agree; the derivative burial record supplies dates and a cemetery locator but no OSS or employment evidence.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable, not settled: an unusual exact name and matching master-sergeant rank agree, but no protected identifier or direct OSS linkage is available in the accessible source.
claims.temporal_assessment: The burial transcription establishes World War II Army service only; it does not establish a pre-OSS employer or immediate assignment.
claims.match_notes: This qualified identity should be tested against Box 569 before elevation to high confidence.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Charles Z Offin is probably the artist, critic, and publisher documented by City College of New York.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact full name and middle initial align, and the institutional biography documents multiple prewar New York art and publishing roles.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable rather than high confidence because the rare exact name agrees but the index supplies no rank, service identifier, birth year, or direct cross-reference.
claims.temporal_assessment: City College documents roles beginning in 1933 and 1937, before the OSS period, but does not describe the transition into OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The biography is presented as a qualified identity; the personnel file remains necessary for confirmation.

claims.claim_text: The probable Charles Z. Offin identity was editor and publisher of Pictures on Exhibit beginning in 1937.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: City College's library biography says Offin edited and published Pictures on Exhibit from 1937 to 1976.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable because the rare exact full name agrees, but no direct OSS personnel-file bridge is available online.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar affiliation beginning in 1937; it is not established as the immediate predecessor to OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The role is published as an earlier documented pre-OSS affiliation, not as a verified immediate employer or last civilian employer.
